name: Red Team Infrastructure & Operations
tagline: Authorized red team tooling: offensive toolkits, operations & reporting, emulation replays, objectives, pivoting, and practice labs.

tools.name: Impacket
tools.desc: Fortra's Python suite for network protocols: SMB/RPC/DCOM/WinRM/Kerberos plus the canonical example scripts (secretsdump, psexec, wmiexec, ntlmrelayx, GetADUsers) for credential harvesting and lateral movement.
tools.when: The workhorse of Windows-lab lateral movement and credential extraction during authorized tests — and the tooling blue teams build artifacts for.

tools.name: NetExec
tools.desc: The maintained successor to CrackMapExec: multi-protocol (SMB/WinRM/LDAP/MSSQL/SSH) networked exploitation toolkit with a plugin system and MCP integration.
tools.when: Fast credential-spraying and share/deployment outreach across a Windows estate in an authorized engagement or AD lab.

tools.name: Responder
tools.desc: lgandx's LLMNR/NBT-NS/mDNS responder that answers name-resolution queries on a test segment to reveal legacy protocol reliance and gather hashes for offline cracking.
tools.when: In a lab or scoped internal test with an explicit rule of engagement, to demonstrate why legacy name-resolution protocols must be disabled.

tools.name: PowerSploit
tools.desc: PowerShellMafia's PowerShell post-exploitation framework (CodeExecution, Recon, Exfiltration, Persistence, Privesc modules). Archived since 2021, yet it remains the canonical documented corpus of PowerShell tradecraft and a rich set of well-known signatures to exercise.
tools.when: Studying classic PowerShell post-exploitation module patterns and testing AMSI/logging detections against well-known tool output.

tools.name: SharpSploit
tools.desc: cobbr's C# post-exploitation library — the compiled mirror of PowerSploit-style tradecraft (execution, persistence, lateral movement, credentialing) for .NET agents.
tools.when: Reference for .NET-based post-exploitation modules and for training why compiled tooling changes the detection story.

tools.name: Nishang
tools.desc: samratashok's collection of PowerShell scripts (reverse shells, keylogging, persistence, scanners) that has historically driven entry-level and small-scope authorized testing.
tools.when: Quick PowerShell payload/auxiliary scripts in a Windows lab without dragging in a full framework.

tools.name: PoC-in-GitHub
tools.desc: nomi-sec's curated index tracking the latest public proof-of-concept exploits by CVE, with cross-references to Exploit-DB, Metasploit, and Nuclei templates.
tools.when: Keep a lab exploitation pipeline current: pull fresh, citation-tracked PoCs to evaluate and adapt in authorized testing.

tools.name: ired.team
tools.desc: The 'red team notes & experiments' GitBook by @spotheplanet — a structured walkthrough of offensive techniques (code execution, injection, persistence, lateral movement) with tool usage and detection notes, documented for education.
tools.when: Read-and-try technique references while building your own lab; the notes pair each experiment with what to look for from a defender's seat.

tools.name: HackTricks
tools.desc: The community wiki of pentesting techniques across web, Windows, Linux, AD, and cloud with tooling recipes and methodology — now maintained as the HackTricks-wiki GitBook project, runnable locally via Docker.
tools.when: Look up a technique or methodology in seconds; the most current single reference for esoteric protocol abuse and tool recipes.

tools.name: RedEye
tools.desc: CISA + PNNL's visual analytic for red-team operations: parses Cobalt Strike and other C2 logs, renders the multi-host attack graph, and supports 'campaign' export for blue-team handoff. Archived to maintenance mode — still the reference for C2 log visualization.
tools.when: Turn raw C2 logs into a shareable, annotated attack-path visualization to debrief stakeholders after an assessment.

tools.name: Ghostwriter
tools.desc: SpecterOps' open-source web application for red-team operations: client tracking, report writing, engagement documents (report templates, infographics), and evidence storage in one place.
tools.when: Run the operational/admin side of a red-team engagement — consistent client documentation, task tracking, and report generation.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/GhostManager/Ghostwriter.git && cd Ghostwriter && docker compose up

tools.name: PwnDoc
tools.desc: Operational reporting tool for keeping engagement notes, screenshots, and CVE references organized, with generated report templates for pentest deliverables.
tools.when: Structure and export aggregated findings and evidence into a client-ready report during or right after an engagement.

tools.name: WriteHat
tools.desc: Black Lantern Security's full-stack Python pentest reporting server with a Django admin and WeasyPrint pipeline that turns structured findings into polished PDF reports.
tools.when: Generate clean PDF deliverables from structured findings without hand-assembling Word templates.

tools.name: MITRE Caldera
tools.desc: Apache Caldera: automated adversary-emulation platform that deploys agents and replays ATT&CK-mapped abilities, letting you re-run a campaign end-to-end and capture artifacts on each pass.
tools.when: Replay the same emulated operation repeatedly after detection changes and measure which signals fire each run.

tools.name: MITRE Attack Flow
tools.desc: Center for Threat-Informed Defense's STIX-based model and toolchain for linking individual ATT&CK techniques into the flow of a full campaign.
tools.when: Document an entire emulated campaign — not isolated techniques — so reporting shows the attack path from initial access to objective.

tools.name: VECTR
tools.desc: Security Risk Advisors' free platform for tracking red/blue test cases and campaign outcomes against MITRE ATT&CK, trending detection coverage over time.
tools.when: Capture objectives and results for each engagement and trend coverage improvements across your program.

tools.name: MITRE ATT&CK Navigator
tools.desc: Web UI for annotating and exploring ATT&CK matrices with shareable layer files — the standard way to plan and communicate engagement objectives.
tools.when: Scope an engagement by marking intended technique coverage, then save the layer for the reporting phase.

tools.name: MITRE ATT&CK
tools.desc: The authoritative knowledge base of adversary tactics, techniques, and data sources — the shared vocabulary for defining engagement objectives.
tools.when: Resolve technique IDs and constraints before planning, and align each engagement's objectives to the matrix.

tools.name: GOAD
tools.desc: Orange Cyberdefense's 'Game of Active Directory' (v3): a vulnerable multi-forest AD lab built with Vagrant/Ansible/Packer, with GOAD-Light and other variants for smaller hardware.
tools.when: An isolated, purpose-built AD domain range for rehearsing the attack paths your toolkits will run in authorized tests.

tools.name: BadBlood
tools.desc: Secframe's PowerShell script that fills a lab AD domain with thousands of randomized users, groups, computers, OUs, and ACLs so lab data resembles a real enterprise.
tools.when: Before practicing enumeration and credential techniques, populate an otherwise empty DC to get realistic object counts and permissions.

tools.name: Metasploitable 3
tools.desc: Rapid7's intentionally vulnerable Windows VM (Vagrant/Packer) packed with unpatched services, weak creds, and web/SMB flaws — a standard target for rehearsing toolkits and C2 staging.
tools.when: A reproducible target for lateral-movement and exploitation run-throughs in an isolated VirtualBox/VMware range.

tools.name: VulnHub
tools.desc: Library of intentionally vulnerable virtual machines and walkthroughs for practicing the full exploratory-to-root workflow at low hardware cost.
tools.when: Practice methodology and tooling against curated vulnerable VMs before applying them to authorized targets.

tools.name: sshuttle
tools.desc: Lightweight VPN-like pivot using SSH; routes traffic through a jump host without requiring root on the target.
tools.when: Need simple, reliable lateral routing to access internal networks from a single jump host during authorized engagements or labs.

tools.name: frp
tools.desc: Fast reverse proxy for exposing local services through a remote server; stable and well-documented.
tools.when: Need controlled reverse proxying for lab infrastructure or authorized test setups behind NAT.

tools.name: proxychains-ng
tools.desc: Force any TCP application through a chain of proxies for controlled routing in authorized testing.
tools.when: Need to route existing tooling through a proxy chain during authorized red team exercises or lab scenarios.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/rofl0r/proxychains-ng && cd proxychains-ng && ./configure --prefix=/usr && make && sudo make install
